newsitem.title: UK: Speculation heats up over Russia debt rating.
newsitem.headline: Speculation heats up over Russia debt rating.

text.p: Speculation over Russia's forthcoming debt rating intensified on Tuesday with traders citing rumours that European rating agency IBCA might announce a BB plus level for the country this week.
"The speculation is that IBCA will release its rating this week -- local sources suggest the rating will be as good as BB plus," said one eastern European debt trader here.

Since Russia announced plans to launch a debut Eurobond before the end of the year, speculation over its foreign currency debt rating has been rife, although BB plus falls just below investment grade.
Talk has focused on whether the major ratings agencies, Moody's and Standard & Poor's, will assign an investment grade or triple B rating for Russia's foreign currency debt.
But a level just below investment grade looks more likely.
"We even think BB plus is a bit racy," said one emerging market debt trader, adding a BB minus rating would be more appropriate.
"Everyone's going to want to see what the big boys are going to do," he added, referring to Moody's and S&P's.
"The Russians have a fantastic ability to pay their debts, but they still have a long way to go."
The Eurobond is expected to emerge at between $300 and $500 million with a three to five-year maturity in November.
Russian ministry of finance officials said last week that ratings were expected in November, though they had previously said a rating would be drawn up by October 10th.
IBCA declined to comment on the market rumours.
JP Morgan and SBC Warburg are lead managing the Eurobond issue and advising Russia on the rating process. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
